theorem.name: Order Invariance / Cost Variance
theorem.statement: For the current additive independent-group model, permuting option-group order preserves the final distinct Pareto objective-vector frontier, while changing cumulative prefix expansion cost.
theorem.reason: Objective addition is commutative, but intermediate Pareto frontier widths depend on which groups have already been composed.

optimizer.method: subset dynamic programming over 2^n subset frontiers
optimizer.edge_cost: number of safe feasible prefix states expanded by adding one group
optimizer.optimality: exact for the frozen expansion-count objective

interpretation: Exact prefix-DP complexity is not only a property of the final problem; it is strongly affected by group composition order.
A locally cheap greedy choice can be globally poor because it ignores how a group reshapes future frontier width.
High-cardinality groups are not necessarily expensive when moved earlier; if the current prefix frontier is narrow, their immediate expansion cost can be much smaller.
The exact order oracle is exponential in group count and is therefore a research oracle/small-n optimizer, not yet a large-n production heuristic.
